svg.title: Plugins: every computation is a row on one kernel; what a result may do is not
svg.desc: Twelve live rows sit round a kernel like the hours of a clock: five signal sources, one data source and six policies. Each provides a service to the kernel, which offers four primitives: provide, inject, effect and event. Three statements follow. Readers ask the kernel for a service by name and never import a plugin. A row that does not mount stops only its own readers and is named. Settlement, the gate and the record are not rows, so no row can change what a result is allowed to do.

text.tspan: Swap what computes. Not what a result is allowed to do.
Every signal, policy and data source is a row. The gate and the record are not.
The brief, the session reports and
the intraday check-ins ask the kernel
for a service. None imports a plugin.
A row that does not mount stops
its own readers and is named.
Settlement, the gate and the record
are not rows. Swapping a row cannot
change what a result may do.
